items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: it was played by The American Composers Orchestra, a very fine new music orchestra in New York, conducted by Dennis Russell Davies

ctx.x: You also had a piece performed at Carnegie Hall, isn’t that right?

Yeah. That was like a further incarnation of some of that NASA work. Basically that was a piece called “Einstein’s Red/Blue Universe,” and it was played by The American Composers Orchestra, a very fine new music orchestra in New York, conducted by Dennis Russell Davies, and it was my first piece for full symphony orchestra and jazz musicians, and sound surround brass choirs in the Carnegie Hall balconies. It was the funniest thing. We had — in order to maximize the use of the musicians there are points in the…
You had to write the time into the piece for how fast the elevator is going up.
